subject: Initial ask: per-1M token IO rates + supported hosted models for POC
messages:
From: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acmeai.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + ask: per-1M token IO rates and model list for hosted API POC

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this. We're standing up a short POC to validate an LLM chat assistant for our enterprise customers. High level: estimate ~12M tokens/month (mix of input/output), peak concurrency low-to-medium. For initial planning the procurement team needs:

- Standard per-1M token rates for input and output (hosted API) across available model tiers (standard / medium / large).
- Which hosted models are currently supported and any notes on latency or recommend-for-chat tags.
- Any quick guidance on when input vs output billing is different for streaming or function-calling.

Also curious about: any starter volume-discount thresholds (e.g., 1M, 10M, 50M tiers) and rough order-of-magnitude on committed pricing vs pay-as-you-go. We're trying to model the budget for a 3-month POC.

Timeline: procurement wants a baseline numbersheet by end of week so we can scope PO. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if easier.

Thanks—
Tom
Tom Jenkins
Head of AI Platform, AcmeAI
From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acmeai.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + ask: per-1M token IO rates and model list for hosted API POC

Tom —

Appreciate the context. I can get you a concise baseline today and a slightly expanded ratecard (with supported-model notes) tomorrow. A few quick clarifying questions so I send the most useful numbers:

- Do you expect the POC to need streaming responses (server-sent events) or standard non-streaming generation?
- Any hard requirements on model families (open models only, or are you ok with Redwood-certified models we host)?
- Is data residency a concern for the POC (we have regional routing options)?

If you prefer, I can include a suggested starter config: 2-3 concurrent endpoints, model A (standard) for lower-latency routing, model B (large) for fallback, plus caching of common prefixes. Call works too — I'm free tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PT.

I'll loop Ben from Sales and Hannah from Pricing so they can add the official numbers and attachments.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intro + ask: per-1M token IO rates and model list for hosted API POC

Tom — looping in Hannah for exact ratecards but a quick, pragmatic baseline for modeling:

- Starter (standard family): $8 / 1M input tokens, $24 / 1M output tokens
- Medium (higher-capacity): $12 / 1M input tokens, $36 / 1M output tokens
- Large (low-latency LLM): $20 / 1M input tokens, $60 / 1M output tokens

Notes:
- These are PAYG (no commit) reference rates for hosted API; committed monthly/annual discounts typically start at 5% for >=10M tokens/month, 12% for >=50M, and custom pricing above 200M.
- Streaming is billed same IO split, but function-calling that emits large structured outputs can push output token counts up — we can show examples.
- We generally recommend caching common prompts or using prefix caching to reduce output volume for assistant scenarios.

Attaching a quick PDF with the starter numbers and model availability. If you can confirm whether you want open-model-only or hybrid (we host some non-open models with certs) I'll adjust the matrix.

Next step: if the numbers look reasonable I can put together a 3-month committed proposal with illustrative discounts.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-hosted-baseline-1M-rates.pdf (stub - see attached PDF for table)

Tom / team —

Attaching two concise artifacts: Redwood_Standard_Ratecard_Q3_2026.pdf (contains IO split tables and common discount tiers) and supported_models_202609.csv (current hosted catalog and recommended tags). TL;DR from the ratecard for quick paste into procurement:

- Standard family: Input $8 / 1M, Output $24 / 1M
- Medium family: Input $12 / 1M, Output $36 / 1M
- Large family (low-latency): Input $20 / 1M, Output $60 / 1M

Discount guidance:
- 5% at 10M/month, 12% at 50M/month, 18% at 200M/month (negotiable for strategic POCs).

Supported models (summary):
- redwood-standard-1 (recommended for chat, ~50–100ms median at our hosted stack)
- redwood-medium-2 (balanced quality/latency)
- redwood-large-x (best quality; higher cost, lower throughput)
- open-moderna, open-vela (community models we host with vetted performance profiles)

A few practical notes:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: billing is still IO-based; streaming may increase perceived latency but does not change token accounting.
- Function-calling: we recommend estimating output token growth (structured outputs) and adding a 20–30% buffer for budgeting.
- If you'd like a short simulation, we can run a tokenization sample against your prompt set and return an expected monthly IO breakdown.

Next steps: I can convert the attachments into an official procurement pack (SOW + PO-ready rates) if you want procurement-friendly formatting. Naomi — if you're scheduling a call, recommend we include a brief run of the supported_models_202609.csv to align on model choice.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Standard_Ratecard_Q3_2026.pdf, supported_models_202609.csv
